novedades.titulo: Triple I (clinical chorioamnionitis): criteria for suspected infection
novedades.fuentes: Subcards 6-20: content from the RPM-SOGOCEP 2025 and RPM-FLASOG 2026 presentations (Dr. Carlos Vera Salerno), verified against the sources cited in each subcard. · Source: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 217 (2020) · Ubom AE, Vatish M, Barnea ER; FIGO. Int J Gynaecol Obstet 2023;163(Suppl 2):40-50 (doi 10.1002/ijgo.15113) · Cowles et al. Obstet Gynecol 1993 (Indigo Carmine vs Methylene Blue) · ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 171 (2016, reaffirmed 2022) · NICE Guideline NG25 (2019, updated 2022) · FIGO Recommendations on Preterm Birth (2021).
novedades.texto: “Triple I” (Intrauterine Inflammation, Infection or both) is the modern term proposed by the 2015 NICHD workshop and adopted by ACOG/SMFM; it replaces “clinical chorioamnionitis” (classic Gibbs 1982 criteria: fever ≥37.8 °C + ≥2 signs; many guidelines use ≥38.0 °C). Definition in ACOG Committee Opinion 712 (2017) Category Criterion Suspected intra-amniotic infection (Triple I) — highest priority Maternal temperature ≥39.0 °C isolated, or 38.0-38.9 °C sustained (confirmed on repeat measurement at 30 min) plus 1 additional factor: maternal leukocytosis, purulent cervical drainage, or fetal tachycardia. Isolated maternal fever Temperature 38.0-38.9 °C without other factors, whether persistent or not. Management of Triple I: broad-spectrum antibiotics, delivery, and maternal resuscitation. In PROM, monitoring uses the same obstetric qSOFA (SBP <90, RR ≥25, altered mental status) used in the sepsis module; ≥2 points = high risk of deterioration. CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 712 (2017) · Medicina Fetal Barcelona — Chorioamnionitis or Triple I.

novedades.fuentes: Revised MUSA (Harmsen MJ et al. UOG 2022;60:118-131) · Van den Bosch 2015 · ESHRE 2022
novedades.texto: Direct features (endometrial tissue in the myometrium): myometrial cysts · hyperechogenic islands · echogenic subendometrial lines and buds. Indirect features (effect on the myometrium): globular uterus · asymmetrical wall thickening · fan-shaped shadowing · translesional vascularity · irregular junctional zone · interrupted junctional zone. Diagnosis: at least one direct feature confirms adenomyosis. Indirect features only: inconclusive; MRI if it changes management. Revised MUSA 2022 advises against diagnosing by junctional zone thickness on ultrasound (the 12 mm cut-off was withdrawn). Report: location (anterior, posterior, fundal, lateral), pattern (diffuse, focal or adenomyoma), layers involved and extent (<25 %, 25–50 %, >50 % of uterine volume). Management: asymptomatic, no treatment. Symptomatic: LNG-IUS, dienogest or combined hormonal contraception, NSAIDs; if no response, GnRH analogues, embolization or selected adenomyomectomy; hysterectomy when childbearing is complete. Wish for pregnancy: refer to reproductive medicine. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Uterus).

novedades.titulo: Infertile couple workup algorithm — Next step by results
novedades.fuentes: WHO 2025 · ASRM 2026 · ESHRE 2023 · AUA/ASRM 2024 · ASRM 2021 (tubal surgery) · RCPI 2023
novedades.texto: CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: WHO 2025, ASRM 2026, ESHRE 2023, AUA/ASRM 2024, ASRM 2021, RCPI 2023. Step 1 — Basic workup in parallel: semen analysis · ovulation (cycle pattern and, if needed, mid-luteal progesterone) · transvaginal ultrasound with AFC · tubal patency (HSG or HyCoSy/HyFoSy) · AMH as appropriate · chlamydia serology as tubal triage (ESHRE). Step 2 — Management by finding: Azoospermia: urology/andrology; FSH, volume and pH; genetics (karyotype, Y microdeletions, CFTR as appropriate); surgical sperm retrieval + ICSI or donor sperm. Male factor by TMSC (CaVeSal® suggestion): >3–5 M → IUI · 1–3 M → IVF · <1 M → ICSI. Bilateral tubal obstruction: IVF/ICSI. Hydrosalpinx: salpingectomy or proximal occlusion before IVF (ASRM 2021). Unilateral: individualize. Anovulation by cause: PMOS → letrozole (first line) · hyperprolactinemia → dopamine agonist · thyroid dysfunction → correct · hypogonadotropic hypogonadism → gonadotropins or pulsatile GnRH · premature ovarian insufficiency → counseling, oocyte donation. Intracavitary pathology (polyp, submucous fibroid, septum, synechiae): hysteroscopy. Cervical factor or sexual dysfunction: IUI (RCPI 2023). The postcoital test is not recommended (ASRM 2026). Low reserve at ≥35 years: do not delay; refer to assisted reproduction. Unexplained infertility (all normal): good prognosis → expectant (WHO 2025: rather than unstimulated IUI; ESHRE 2023); poor prognosis → IUI with ovarian stimulation for 3–6 cycles → IVF. Infections: chlamydia and gonorrhea by risk, treating both partners. Mycoplasma and Ureaplasma: no guideline (ASRM, ESHRE, WHO) supports routine testing in infertility; only with clinical findings (cervicitis, urethritis, PID). See "Chlamydia, Mycoplasma genitalium and Ureaplasma". Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Couple workup): pressing Calculate shows the next step.

novedades.fuentes: ASRM Committee Opinion (2026) · ASRM (2021) · WHO 2025 · ESHRE 2023
novedades.texto: When to evaluate: no pregnancy after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse (<35 years), after 6 months (≥35 years) and immediately after 40 or with a known cause (oligo/amenorrhea, endometriosis, PID, pelvic surgery, chemo- or radiotherapy, known male factor). Evaluate both partners in parallel. Pillars: (1) Ovarian — regular 21–35-day cycles suggest ovulation; with irregular cycles confirm with mid-luteal progesterone (WHO 2025) and look for the cause with a hormonal profile (FSH, estradiol, prolactin, TSH, androgens). Reserve with AMH and AFC. (2) Tubal — HSG or HyCoSy/HyFoSy (equivalent); with high risk (chlamydia or PID, endometriosis, pelvic surgery, ectopic) consider laparoscopy with chromopertubation. (3) Uterine — transvaginal ultrasound, ideally 3D; suspected intracavitary lesion → sonohysterography or hysteroscopy. Not routine (ASRM 2026): postcoital test, TSH and prolactin without clinical indication, thrombophilia testing and karyotype. Next step by results: see "Infertile couple workup algorithm". Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Couple workup).

novedades.titulo: Integrated algorithm — GLP-1/GIP and reproductive planning
novedades.fuentes: Synthesis of the guides in this same section: Contraception during tirzepatide, Preconception washout by molecule, Inadvertent pregnancy during GLP-1/tirzepatide, Metformin in pregnancy, GLP-1 and fertility recovery
novedades.texto: Branch 1 — Patient on GLP-1/GIP treatment who is NOT seeking pregnancy (or has not yet decided): Active contraceptive counseling from the start of treatment, even if she previously had anovulation due to PMOS (see the GLP-1 and fertility recovery guide) — fertility can recover before the patient notices. Prefer non-oral methods (LARC, injectable, patch, ring), especially with tirzepatide; if she uses an oral method, add a barrier method for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose escalation (see the Contraception during tirzepatide guide). Branch 2 — Patient who IS seeking pregnancy (preconception planning): Washout by molecule before attempting to conceive (see the Preconception washout by molecule guide) — semaglutide ≥2 months, tirzepatide ≥1 month (European/UK label), extended-release exenatide ≥3 months; no validated interval for liraglutide, dulaglutide, short-acting exenatide or lixisenatide; retatrutide does not apply, as it is not approved. Reassess baseline metabolic management (metformin, myo-inositol) in a preconception context, not a weight-loss one (see the Metformin in pregnancy and Myo-inositol guides). Preconception folic acid according to risk level (see the Preconception screening and folic acid guide). Branch 3 — Inadvertent pregnancy already confirmed during GLP-1/GIP use: Stop the drug immediately. Reassess the metabolic plan in a pregnancy context, not a weight-loss one (see the Inadvertent pregnancy during GLP-1/tirzepatide guide). Discuss the available evidence with the patient — reassuring regarding malformations, more mixed regarding gestational weight gain/gestational diabetes/hypertension (see the same guide) — without creating unwarranted alarm or false reassurance. 5 key messages for counseling: GLP-1/GIP-slowed gastric emptying can reduce absorption of oral contraceptives — discuss it proactively, not reactively. Fertility recovery from weight loss can occur before the patient notices the menstrual change. Preconception washout varies by molecule — there is no single rule for "the GLP-1s." Facing an inadvertent pregnancy, stopping the drug is the immediate step — evidence on malformations is reassuring so far, but evidence on maternal metabolic/hypertensive outcomes is more mixed and warrants active pregnancy follow-up, not just reassurance. The real teratogen in diabetes is uncontrolled hyperglycemia, not the drug itself — do not stop an antidiabetic agent without an already-defined replacement plan.

novedades.fuentes: ISUOG 2024 · SMFM #46 · ACOG PB 229 (2021)

Polyhydramnios: maternal (diabetes) · fetal (GI, CNS, neuromuscular, cardiac, chromosomal) · membrane-related (TTTS recipient) · idiopathic 50-60%.

novedades.fuentes: ISUOG Practice Guidelines (2024, Khalil) · SMFM Consult Series #46 — Polyhydramnios (2018, reaf. 2024) · ACOG Practice Bulletin 229 (2021) · Phelan 1987
novedades.texto: Methods: SDP/DVP (preferred) · AFI (4 quadrants). Classic: Oligohydramnios AFI<5/SDP<2 · Normal 5.1-24.9/2.1-7.9 · Polyhydramnios AFI≥25/SDP≥8. Borderline ranges (lower zone: Phelan 1987; upper zone: CaVeSal® suggestion): Anhydramnios=0 · Severe <1/<3 · Lower borderline 5.1-8.0 (follow-up) · Physiological normal 8.1-18.0 · Upper borderline 18.1-24.9.

novedades.titulo: Threatened preterm labor (TPL) — Diagnosis and tocolysis
novedades.fuentes: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 171 (2016, reaffirmed 2022) · NICE NG25 (2019, updated 2022) · FIGO Recommendations on Preterm Birth (2021)
novedades.texto: Diagnosis: regular uterine dynamics (≥4/20min) + cervical changes, 22-36+6 wk. TVUS: CL >30mm rules out TPL · CL <25mm high risk · 20-30mm → biomarkers (fetal fibronectin/PAMG-1). Tocolysis (22/24-33+6 wk): Nifedipine (1st line) loading dose 10-20mg q20min → maintenance q6-8h · Atosiban (NICE/RCOG) · Indomethacin (before wk 32, do not combine with MgSO4 or nifedipine).

novedades.fuentes: AACE/ACE · Endocrine Society · SURMOUNT/STEP · Austin GO, et al. Front Mol Biosci 2023;10:1170181 · Davies M, et al. Lancet 2021;397(10278):971-984 · Rubino D, et al. JAMA 2021;325(14):1414-1425 (STEP 4) · Aronne LJ, et al. JAMA 2024;331(1):38-48 (SURMOUNT-4) · Castaneda R, et al. The Lancet Obstetrics, Gynaecology, & Women's Health. 2026;2(2):e118-e128. doi:10.1016/S3050-5038(25)00145-1 · Wilding JPH, et al. Diabetes Obes Metab 2022;24(8):1553-1564 (STEP 1 extension) · Hurtado Andrade MD. Menopause 2024;31:737-739 · The Menopause Society 2026, congress abstract (preliminary)
novedades.texto: Semaglutide 0.25→2.4mg/wk. Tirzepatide 2.5→10-15mg/wk. Indication: BMI≥30, or ≥27+comorbidity. ⚠️ "Ozempic babies" (restores ovulation), reduces OCP efficacy, stop before trying to conceive according to the molecule (semaglutide ≥2 months; tirzepatide ≥1 month per the European/UK label; see Preconception washout by molecule guide), risk of sarcopenia. Non-response rates (<5% weight loss) by pivotal trial: STEP-1 (semaglutide 2.4mg, non-diabetic adults) 13.6% · STEP-TEENS (semaglutide 2.4mg, adolescents with excess-weight comorbidity) 27% · SURMOUNT-1 (tirzepatide 15mg, non-diabetic adults) 9% · STEP-2 (semaglutide 2.4mg, diabetic adults) 31.2% — response is consistently lower in patients with concomitant type 2 diabetes, a point to anticipate when counseling on expectations. Maintaining weight loss requires continuing the medication (STEP 4 with semaglutide and SURMOUNT-4 with tirzepatide): in both trials, patients who, on reaching a weight-loss plateau, were randomized to continue the drug maintained or further deepened their weight loss, while those switched to placebo progressively regained weight over the remaining follow-up — obesity behaves here as a chronic condition requiring sustained treatment, not as a short course with a permanent outcome. Figures: STEP 4 (Rubino 2021), weeks 20-68: −7.9% with semaglutide vs. +6.9% with placebo; SURMOUNT-4 (Aronne, JAMA 2024;331(1):38-48), weeks 36-88: −5.5% with tirzepatide vs. +14.0% with placebo. STEP 1 extension (Wilding, Diabetes Obes Metab 2022; n=327): after −17.3% at week 68, stopping led to regain of 11.6 percentage points by week 120, about two-thirds of the weight lost. GLP-1/GIP + hormone therapy in the climacteric (retrospective cohort, Mayo Clinic): Castaneda et al. (The Lancet Obstetrics, Gynaecology, & Women's Health. 2026;2(2):e118-e128), in 120 postmenopausal women with overweight/obesity on tirzepatide (40 on HRT vs. 80 without, propensity-matched), reported that at 15 months total body weight loss was 19.2% with concomitant HRT vs. 14.0% without HRT (p=0.0023), about 35% more; the HRT group also showed additional improvements in diastolic blood pressure, triglycerides and AST. ⚠️ This is retrospective matched-cohort evidence, not a randomized trial — it suggests a possible synergy but does not establish causality, nor does it by itself change the indication for HRT, which should be decided on its own criteria (see the MRS Scale and HRT guide). Note: the ENDO 2025 abstract reported 17% vs. 14% at last follow-up; the final publication reports 19.2% vs. 14.0%, which is the figure used in this guide. Preliminary (congress abstract, The Menopause Society 2026): in a larger cohort, the association between HRT and greater weight loss was sustained with semaglutide; with tirzepatide it was early only and later no longer significant. ⚠️ Abstract without full peer-reviewed publication — does not change management. Menopause 2026 abstracts Menopause-transition context (Hurtado Andrade MD. Menopause 2024;31:737-739): according to SWAN, during the transition fat-mass gain increases 2.5-fold and lean-mass loss 3-fold. This is a review article, not a trial.

novedades.titulo: Cervical cancer — Screening and management algorithm (ASCCP)
novedades.fuentes: ASCCP 2019 (Perkins et al., 2020) · J Low Genit Tract Dis 2024;28:3-6 · ASCCP enduring guidelines 2024-2025
novedades.texto: Age: <21 none · 21-29 Pap every 3 years · 30-65 primary hrHPV every 5 years (preferred), co-test every 5 or Pap every 3 · >65 stop if adequate prior screening. HIV or immunosuppression: special schedule. Management by result: negative HPV or co-test → 5 years · HPV 16/18 → colposcopy even with NILM · other HPV + NILM → repeat in 1 year · ASC-US + HPV negative → 3 years · ASC-US + HPV positive → colposcopy (<25 years: cytology in 1 year) · LSIL ≥25 → colposcopy (<25: cytology in 1 year) · ASC-H → colposcopy always · HSIL ≥25 → expedited excision or colposcopy (<25: colposcopy) · AGC → colposcopy + endocervical sampling + endometrial sampling if ≥35 or at risk · AIS → diagnostic excision · carcinoma → biopsy and gynecologic oncology. 2024-2025 updates: p16/Ki-67 dual stain for HPV-positive triage (positive → colposcopy; negative → HPV in 1 year). Self-collected vaginal HPV accepted: 16/18 → colposcopy; other types → clinician-collected sample for cytology; negative → repeat in 3 years. Extended genotyping: use the ASCCP app for exact risk. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Breast, cervix and endometrium). ASCCP enduring guidelines.

novedades.fuentes: FIGO 2018 (Bhatla N et al. IJGO 2019;145:129-135) · ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2023
novedades.texto: I confined to the cervix: IA1 invasion ≤3 mm · IA2 >3–5 mm · IB1 ≤2 cm · IB2 >2–4 cm · IB3 >4 cm. II beyond the uterus, not lower third of vagina or pelvic wall: IIA1 upper vagina, tumor ≤4 cm · IIA2 >4 cm · IIB parametria. III IIIA lower third of vagina · IIIB pelvic wall or hydronephrosis · IIIC1 pelvic nodes · IIIC2 para-aortic nodes (r imaging, p pathology; nodes define IIIC regardless of tumor size). IV IVA bladder or rectal mucosa (biopsy) · IVB distant metastasis. Management (ESGO 2023): pelvic MRI mandatory; PET-CT or CT for IB3 or higher (except IIA1) or suspicious nodes. IA1 without LVSI: conization or simple hysterectomy. IA1 with LVSI or IA2: add sentinel node. IB1–IIA1: radical hysterectomy with pelvic nodes, open approach; radical trachelectomy if IB1 and fertility desired. IB3 and IIA2–IVA: platinum chemoradiation plus brachytherapy. IVB: systemic. Always gynecologic oncology. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Oncology).

novedades.fuentes: FIGO 2023 (Berek JS et al. IJGO 2023;162:383-394) · ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2025 (Lancet Oncol 2025) · ESGO/ESHRE/ESGE 2023
novedades.texto: Histotypes: non-aggressive = grade 1–2 endometrioid. Aggressive = grade 3 endometrioid, serous, clear cell, undifferentiated, mixed, mesonephric-like, gastrointestinal mucinous, carcinosarcoma. I (uterus, non-aggressive without substantial LVSI): IA1 endometrium or polyp · IA2 invasion <50 % · IA3 low-grade limited to uterus and ovary (unilateral, no rupture, <50 %, no substantial LVSI) · IB ≥50 % · IC aggressive limited to endometrium or polyp. II IIA cervical stroma (non-aggressive) · IIB substantial LVSI (non-aggressive) · IIC aggressive with myometrial invasion. III IIIA1 ovary or tube · IIIA2 serosa · IIIB1 vagina or parametria · IIIB2 pelvic peritoneum · IIIC1 pelvic nodes (i micro, ii macro) · IIIC2 para-aortic (i, ii). IV IVA bladder or bowel mucosa · IVB abdominal peritoneum beyond the pelvis · IVC distant metastasis. Molecular group in I–II: POLEmut → IAm POLEmut · p53abn with myometrial invasion → IICm p53abn · MMRd and NSMP are recorded. In III–IV the stage does not change. Management: molecular classification in all; MMRd → Lynch testing. Pelvic MRI or expert ultrasound; CT if high risk. Hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and sentinel node. IAm POLEmut and low risk: no adjuvant therapy. IICm p53abn: chemotherapy ± radiotherapy. III–IVA: surgery plus systemic therapy (immunotherapy especially in MMRd) ± radiotherapy. IVB–IVC: systemic. Fertility preservation: low-grade IA1 in a referral center. Always gynecologic oncology. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Oncology).

novedades.fuentes: CaVeSal® summary based on AJCC 8th ed. (anatomic and prognostic stage) · NCCN · ESMO 2024
novedades.texto: T (size): Tis in situ · T1 up to 2 cm · T2 more than 2 and up to 5 cm · T3 more than 5 cm · T4 chest wall or skin (includes inflammatory carcinoma). N (nodes): N0 none · N1 mobile ipsilateral axillary · N2 fixed axillary or internal mammary · N3 infraclavicular, supraclavicular or axillary with internal mammary. M: M0 no metastasis · M1 distant metastasis. Prognostic stage: AJCC 8th ed. adds grade, estrogen and progesterone receptors, HER2 and, when available, genomic assay; the stage may go up or down versus the anatomic stage. For the exact stage, use the AJCC manual. Management: asymptomatic stage I–II: no routine staging imaging. Stage III, symptoms or abnormal labs: contrast CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis plus bone scan, or PET-CT. Breast MRI in selected cases. Genetic counseling by criteria (BRCA). Treatment by a multidisciplinary breast team. CaVeSal® original summary; does not reproduce AJCC tables.

novedades.fuentes: FIGO 2014 (Prat J. IJGO 2014;124:1-5) · ESGO-ESMO-ESP 2024 (Ann Oncol 2024;35:248-266)
novedades.texto: I ovaries or tubes: IA one · IB both · IC1 surgical spill · IC2 rupture before surgery or surface tumor · IC3 malignant cells in ascites or washings. II pelvis: IIA uterus or tubes · IIB other pelvic tissues. III IIIA1 retroperitoneal nodes only (i ≤10 mm, ii >10 mm) · IIIA2 microscopic extrapelvic peritoneum · IIIB macroscopic ≤2 cm · IIIC >2 cm (includes liver and spleen capsule). IV IVA pleural effusion with positive cytology · IVB parenchymal or extra-abdominal metastases (includes inguinal nodes). Management (ESGO-ESMO-ESP 2024): contrast CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis; CA-125 and CEA. Germline and somatic BRCA in high-grade non-mucinous of any stage, HRD in stage III–IV BRCA wild-type, genetic counseling. I–II: complete staging surgery; fertility-sparing in selected cases; adjuvant platinum except low-grade IA–IB. III–IV: primary cytoreduction to no residual disease or neoadjuvant chemotherapy and interval surgery; maintenance by BRCA/HRD (PARP inhibitors, bevacizumab). Imaging alone does not decide resectability. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Oncology).

novedades.fuentes: POP-Q (Bump RC et al. AJOG 1996) · ICS/IUGA (Haylen BT et al. 2016) · NICE NG123 (2019) · ACOG/AUGS PB 214 (2019) · FDA 2019 (malla transvaginal)
novedades.texto: POP-Q: points Aa, Ba (anterior), C (cervix or vault), D (posterior fornix), Ap, Bp (posterior) in cm relative to the hymen (0; negative above, positive below); genital hiatus, perineal body and total vaginal length (TVL). Stage 0 no prolapse · I most distal point <−1 cm · II between −1 and +1 cm · III >+1 cm but not beyond TVL −2 cm · IV complete eversion. Management: asymptomatic, watchful waiting. Symptoms: pelvic floor muscle training for 16 weeks, pessary (ring or Gellhorn) with follow-up; postmenopause: vaginal estriol to improve tolerance. Surgery if this fails or by preference: anterior colporrhaphy; apical sacrospinous or uterosacral suspension, or sacrocolpopexy; posterior colporrhaphy. Not sexually active and high surgical risk: colpocleisis. Transvaginal mesh for anterior repair withdrawn by the FDA (2019). Look for occult stress incontinence by reducing the prolapse. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Prolapse).

novedades.fuentes: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 13. Management of Menopause-Related Vasomotor, Sleep, and Mood Symptoms. Obstet Gynecol. 2026;148(5):e345-e369
novedades.texto: Interventions with supporting evidence for vasomotor symptoms (VMS), sleep disturbance and mood symptoms of the climacteric — all recommended as adjuncts to hormonal or non-hormonal pharmacologic therapy, not as first-line substitutes when pharmacologic treatment is indicated: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT): improves VMS, sleep and mood (conditional recommendation, low-to-moderate-quality evidence). Can be delivered in person, by phone, or online. Mindfulness-based interventions (meditation, body scanning, breathing exercises, yoga): improve sleep and mood (conditional recommendation, low-to-moderate-quality evidence); usual duration 8 weeks in the trials. Physical exercise: improves sleep and mood (conditional recommendation, low-to-moderate-quality evidence); greatest sleep benefit with 70-90 minute sessions. Clinical hypnosis: reduces VMS and improves sleep and anxiety symptoms (conditional recommendation, low-quality evidence); weekly 45-minute sessions or self-hypnosis programs with a daily 20-minute recording. Acupuncture: reduces VMS and improves sleep and mood (conditional recommendation, low-quality evidence); high heterogeneity across protocols, most trials conducted in China. ⚠️ Natural products and supplements — NOT recommended: the available evidence does not support the efficacy or safety of phytoestrogens (e.g., soy isoflavones) or herbal supplements for the treatment of vasomotor or menopausal symptoms — limited by small sample sizes and heterogeneity of formulations/doses/durations across trials. Since they are not FDA-regulated or evaluated for safety/purity as nutritional supplements, no leading international guideline (ACOG, NAMS/The Menopause Society, IMS) includes them among recommended treatment options.

novedades.fuentes: USPSTF (2023) · ACOG CO 762 (2019)
novedades.texto: Basic labs + serologies + Pap/mammogram as appropriate. Folic acid: standard 400mcg/day · high risk 4 mg/day (ACOG/CDC) or 5 mg/day (NICE/RCOG) up to wk 12 (prior NTD in the woman or partner, diabetes, obesity, epilepsy or anticonvulsants). MTHFR: standard folic acid at the same dose (CDC). It is the only form of folate shown to prevent neural tube defects; methylfolate (5-MTHF) does not replace it. MTHFR testing is not recommended (ACMG 2013, reaffirmed in 2020). Paraguay context (MSPyBS): the official public health communication from Paraguay's Ministry of Public Health and Welfare (MSPyBS) recommends 0.5mg (500mcg)/day as the standard preconception/gestational folic acid dose — slightly higher than the international 400mcg standard cited above, without changing the high-risk dose (4-5mg/day) in the risk scenarios already described. The MSPyBS Manual Nacional de Normas de Cuidados: Preconcepcional, Prenatal, Parto, Nacimiento y Puerperio; Seguros e Inclusivos (3rd ed. 2022; Resolución S.G. N.º 1078/2021, already cited elsewhere in this guide section for the PBF re-evaluation window) structures the preconception visit as "traffic-light" (semáforo), i.e. tiered by risk level — confirmed that this scheme exists in the official document.

novedades.fuentes: CLAP-PAHO/WHO
novedades.texto: Pregnancy lasts, on average, 280 days (40 weeks) from the first day of the LMP — 9 calendar months or 10 lunar months. Always expressed in completed weeks. Rules to estimate EDD: Wahl (LMP+10 days, -3 months) · Naegele (LMP+7 days, -3 months) · Pinard (last day of menstruation+10 days, -3 months; the least used). In the medical record the EDD is calculated with Naegele or Wahl and is always editable; Pinard appears only as a reference in this guide. Ultrasound correction: if it differs beyond the accepted margin, GA by ultrasound takes priority — the earlier the scan, the more reliable (maximum precision in the 1st trimester).

novedades.titulo: Inadvertent pregnancy during GLP-1/tirzepatide — what the evidence shows
novedades.fuentes: Brown ME, et al. GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use During the Periconceptional Period, Ann Intern Med (2026) — target trial emulation, n=3,572 · D'Antonio F, et al. Periconceptional and early pregnancy exposure to GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists and obstetric/neonatal outcomes, Med (2026) — meta-analysis, n=2,118,215 · AJOG 2024 (review), PII S0002-9378(24)00864-0 · Uysal N, et al. Pregnancy outcomes following maternal GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Sci Rep. 2026;16:31416 · Liu X, et al. Periconceptional use of GLP-1 receptor agonists and the risk of major congenital malformations: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Endocr Connect. 2026;15(7). DOI 10.1530/EC-26-0280 · Maya J, et al. Gestational Weight Gain and Pregnancy Outcomes After GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Discontinuation. JAMA. 2025;334(24):2186-2196. DOI 10.1001/jama.2025.20951 · Pondugula N, et al. Gestational Weight Gain and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy With Prepregnancy and Early Pregnancy GLP-1RA Exposure. Obstet Gynecol. 2026;147(3):293-302. DOI 10.1097/AOG.0000000000005995
novedades.texto: Immediate management of an inadvertent pregnancy in a patient using GLP-1/GIP: Stop the drug as soon as pregnancy is confirmed — current evidence does not support continuing it during gestation, regardless of the duration of periconceptional exposure that has already occurred. Reassess the patient's overall metabolic management plan (glycemia, weight, possible metformin indication — see corresponding guide) now in the context of pregnancy, not of weight loss. There is no indication for pregnancy termination based solely on periconceptional GLP-1/GIP exposure — the conversation with the patient should be grounded in the available evidence (summarized below), which so far shows no consistent signal of harm. What the evidence shows (quick-reference summary, not a substitute for each study's methodological detail): Brown et al. (Ann Intern Med 2026, target trial emulation, n=3,572) found no significant increase in major congenital malformations associated with periconceptional exposure to GLP-1 agonists, using a design that emulates a randomized trial from observational data to reduce confounding by indication. Major congenital malformations: adjusted prevalence ratio 1.21 (95% CI 0.83-1.82); non-live birth: adjusted RR 1.09 (Ann Intern Med 2026;179(7):929-937). Wide intervals: a moderate effect cannot be excluded. D'Antonio et al. (Med 2026, large-scale meta-analysis, n=2,118,215) likewise found no consistent signal of increased risk of adverse obstetric/neonatal outcomes associated with periconceptional or early-pregnancy exposure to GLP-1/GIP agonists — this being the largest sample-size analysis available to date on the topic. The AJOG 2024 review (PII S0002-9378(24)00864-0) synthesizes the body of evidence available at that time in the same reassuring direction, although — like the rest of this literature — it is based predominantly on observational studies rather than randomized trials specifically designed to assess reproductive safety. ⚠️ All of this evidence is observational (cohorts, target trial emulation, cohort meta-analyses) — absence of a harm signal is not equivalent to definitive evidence of safety, and it does not change the recommendation to stop the drug as soon as pregnancy is recognized, nor the recommendation to respect the preconception washout by molecule when pregnancy is planned (see the Preconception washout by molecule guide). Malformations — additional meta-analysis (Uysal et al., Sci Rep 2026;16:31416): across 7 cohort studies with over 40,000 exposed pregnancies, there was no significant signal for congenital malformations overall (OR 1.11; 95% CI 0.82-1.51) nor for major malformations with first-trimester exposure (OR 1.39; 95% CI 0.73-2.65). An isolated significant signal was found for urinary malformations (OR 1.24; 95% CI 1.05-1.47), based on unadjusted data from only 2 studies — the authors themselves attribute it most likely to residual confounding (underlying maternal diabetes/obesity), not a direct teratogenic effect. No increased signal was found for stillbirth, spontaneous abortion, small for gestational age, or preterm birth. Major congenital malformations — largest sample-size meta-analysis available to date (Liu X, et al. Endocrine Connections 2026;15(7). DOI 10.1530/EC-26-0280): across 6 studies (1 prospective + 5 retrospective) with 286,599 women, of whom 43,577 had periconceptional GLP-1RA exposure, there was no significant difference in the risk of major congenital malformations between exposed and unexposed women (RR 1.02; 95% CI 0.96-1.08). No significant signal was found either for preterm birth (RR 1.09; 95% CI 0.80-1.49), large for gestational age (RR 2.31; 95% CI 0.56-9.44), small for gestational age (RR 0.71; 95% CI 0.39-1.27), or stillbirth (RR 1.16; 95% CI 0.24-5.69) — these last three have very wide confidence intervals due to low event numbers, and should be read as "insufficient statistical power to detect a risk if one existed," not as "no risk." The authors themselves note that, given the observational design and limited number of exposed pregnancies, these findings should not be interpreted as proof of safety. Gestational weight gain and complications after stopping the drug (Maya J, et al. JAMA 2025;334(24):2186-2196 — retrospective cohort, Mass General Brigham, n=448 exposed vs. 1,344 unexposed, matched by propensity score 1:3, 84% with obesity): exposure to GLP-1/GIP between 3 years before and 90 days after conception was associated with greater gestational weight gain (mean 13.7kg vs. 10.5kg; difference +3.3kg; 95% CI 2.3-4.2; p<0.001), a higher risk of excess gestational weight gain (65% vs. 49%; RR 1.32; 95% CI 1.19-1.47), of preterm delivery (17% vs. 13%; RR 1.34; 95% CI 1.06-1.69), of gestational diabetes (20% vs. 15%; RR 1.30; 95% CI 1.01-1.68), and of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (46% vs. 36%; RR 1.29; 95% CI 1.12-1.49) — with no difference in birth length, large/small for gestational age, or cesarean delivery. ⚠️ Unlike Liu et al. (above), which looks for a malformation signal, this cohort looks at the pregnant patient's own metabolic/hypertensive outcomes after periconceptional exposure — a different, and to some extent contrasting, perspective to the reassurance conveyed by Imbroane et al. 2025 (see the Preconception washout by molecule guide): "no malformation signal" does not equal "no maternal risk at all." Cohort composed mostly of women with obesity — limits generalization to a non-obese population. Gestational weight gain and hypertensive disorders — independent cohort (Pondugula N, et al. Obstet Gynecol. 2026;147(3):293-302. DOI 10.1097/AOG.0000000000005995): a retrospective cohort distinct from Maya et al. (Yale, n=243 exposed up to 1 year before pregnancy — 103 for pregestational diabetes, 140 for weight management — vs. 175 and 200 unexposed, respectively). Found no association between GLP-1RA exposure and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy in either cohort (pregestational diabetes: adjusted OR 0.72; 95% CI 0.42-1.25 · weight management: adjusted OR 0.83; 95% CI 0.45-1.52). There was also no association with gestational weight gain in the pregestational diabetes cohort; in the weight-management cohort, exposure was associated with a lower likelihood of gestational weight gain below recommendations (adjusted OR 0.37; 95% CI 0.18-0.78) — the authors interpret this as a possible rebound weight gain after stopping the drug, not as excess weight gain. ⚠️ Important attribution note: the figures of 65% vs. 49% excess weight gain, 20% vs. 15% gestational diabetes, and 46% vs. 36% hypertensive disorders (above) belong to Maya et al., not to this study — these are two independent cohorts with different findings (Pondugula et al. reports no hypertensive-disorder signal; Maya et al. does).

novedades.fuentes: ESHRE Guideline (Becker CM et al. Hum Reprod Open 2022) · IDEA (Guerriero S et al. UOG 2016) · #Enzian (Keckstein J et al. Acta Obstet Gynecol Scand 2021) · rASRM (Fertil Steril 1997) · EFI (Adamson GD, Pasta DJ. Fertil Steril 2010) · Benaglia L, et al. AJOG 2026
novedades.texto: Suspicion: dysmenorrhoea not relieved by NSAIDs, deep dyspareunia, cyclic dyschezia or dysuria, chronic pelvic pain, infertility. Transvaginal ultrasound with the IDEA approach (4 steps): uterus and adnexa (endometrioma, adenomyosis) · soft markers (fixed ovaries, site-specific tenderness) · pouch of Douglas sliding sign · deep nodules by compartment. Negative ultrasound or MRI does not rule it out; empirical treatment without laparoscopy is acceptable. #Enzian 2021 (by ultrasound u, MRI m or surgery s): P peritoneum · O endometrioma left/right · T tubo-ovarian adhesions left/right · A vagina/rectovaginal septum · B uterosacral ligaments/parametria left/right · C rectum · F: FA adenomyosis, FB bladder, FU ureter, FI other bowel, FO other. Grades 1 (<1 cm) · 2 (1–3 cm) · 3 (>3 cm). Example: #Enzian(u) O2/0 A1 B2/0 C1 FA. rASRM (surgical): I minimal 1–5 · II mild 6–15 · III moderate 16–40 · IV severe >40. It does not predict pain or pregnancy. EFI (after surgery, if pregnancy is desired): age, years of infertility, prior pregnancy, least function of tubes, fimbriae and ovaries (LF), rASRM lesion and total scores. 0–10 points: higher means better spontaneous pregnancy rate. Low EFI or male factor: assisted reproduction. Management (ESHRE 2022): pain: NSAIDs, continuous combined contraceptive, progestogens (dienogest 2 mg/day, desogestrel 75 mcg/day, levonorgestrel IUD 52 mg), second line GnRH agonists or antagonists with add-back (relugolix 40 mg + estradiol 1 mg + norethisterone acetate 0.5 mg/day). Surgery if treatment fails or is contraindicated; endometrioma: cystectomy. Infertility: endometrioma, no routine surgery before IVF, measure AMH. Deep disease: surgery or IVF according to pain, age and ovarian reserve. Infertility with ultrasound-diagnosed ovarian or deep endometriosis: a small trial (Benaglia 2026; 55 randomized and 75 preference-cohort women, stopped early) favored IVF over surgery: live births 57% vs. 26% in the randomized cohort (RR 2.20). Preliminary evidence. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Endometriosis).

novedades.fuentes: WHO Guideline (2025) — WHO's first guideline on the subject
novedades.texto: Careful history/exam to choose studies. Essential female evaluation in parallel. Counseling on tobacco+STIs. Document outcomes. Psychosocial support. Key points for the workup (WHO 2025, 40 recommendations): ovulation by mid-luteal progesterone rather than serial ultrasound tracking · tubal patency by HSG or HyCoSy · abnormal semen analysis: repeat at 11 weeks or later · unexplained infertility: expectant management rather than unstimulated IUI · PMOS with anovulation: letrozole as first line. Next step by results: see "Infertile couple workup algorithm".

novedades.titulo: MRS scale and Hormone Replacement Therapy
novedades.fuentes: NAMS Position Statement (2022) · Heinemann et al. (2004) · Manual para Manejo de la Mujer en Edad del Climaterio, 2nd ed. (SOCHEG, 2020) · Stute P, et al. EMAS 2026 framework, Maturitas 2026;212:109060 · MSPyBS Paraguay Res. S.G. No. 267/2023 · ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 13. Management of Menopause-Related Vasomotor, Sleep, and Mood Symptoms. Obstet Gynecol. 2026;148(5):e345-e369 · Qaseem A, et al. ACP. Ann Intern Med 2026. doi:10.7326/ANNALS-26-01205
novedades.texto: MRS (11 items): somatic, psychological, urogenital. Heinemann 2004 scheme (HQLO 2:67; total and by domain, the one CaVeSal® adopts): total 0-4 no/little symptoms · 5-8 mild · 9-15 moderate · ≥16 severe (consider HRT); somatic 0-2 · 3-4 · 5-7 · ≥8; psychological 0-1 · 2-3 · 4-6 · ≥7; urogenital 0 · 1 · 2-3 · ≥4. Variant from the methodological review (HQLO 2:45, Table 6): total moderate 9-16 / severe ≥17 and somatic moderate 5-8 / severe ≥9 (psychological and urogenital the same). SOCHEG scheme (broken down by domain, each with its own severe-alteration cutoff): Somatic (items 1-4) ≥8 · Psychological (items 5-8) ≥6 · Urogenital (items 9-11) ≥3 · Total (items 1-11) ≥15. HRT by uterine status: no uterus → estrogen alone. Uterus present, perimenopause → sequential/cyclic. Postmenopause → continuous combined. Transdermal HRT (preferred, especially with hypertension, obesity BMI>30, hypertriglyceridemia, VTE risk): 17β-Estradiol gel 0.75-1.25g/day, or patches 25-50mcg/day. Endometrial protection (intact uterus): Micronized natural progesterone 200mg/day for 10-14 days/month (sequential regimen) or 100mg/day continuous · or Dydrogesterone 10-20mg/day. Tibolone (STEAR): 2.5mg/day PO (or 1.25mg/day in lower body weight or advanced perimenopause) — covers vasomotor symptoms, urogenital atrophy and bone loss prevention (estrogen doses to prevent bone loss and what to do when MHT is stopped: see Osteoporosis and bone densitometry); does not require an added progestogen. Tissue-selective estrogen complex (alternative when avoiding a progestogen is preferred): Conjugated equine estrogens 0.45mg/day + Bazedoxifene 20mg/day — bazedoxifene (a SERM) replaces the progestogen for endometrial protection, without the bleeding or breast tenderness associated with it. Evidence from the SMART-1/SMART-2 trials (12 weeks): significant reduction in hot flush frequency/severity vs. placebo, with a 50% reduction by day 8-10 and a sustained ~90% reduction by day 83 of use; no increased risk of breast cancer, endometrial cancer, VTE, stroke or coronary disease in pooled analyses (follow-up up to 2 years — confidence limited by low event incidence and lack of longer-term data). ⚠️ Availability in Paraguay not confirmed — verify locally before prescribing. Alternative endometrial protection — 52mg LNG-IUD: off-label use alongside systemic estrogen to provide endometrial protection (plus contraception if applicable) — replace at 5 years when used for this purpose (the approved contraceptive lifespan is 8 years, but the evidence supporting endometrial protection in HRT covers up to 5 years). Local availability (Paraguay, confirm against the current pharmacy/distributor): transdermal 17β-estradiol gel/spray (e.g., Ginoderm) — available. 17β-estradiol vaginal ring — not available. Conjugated equine estrogens + bazedoxifene — availability unconfirmed. This information is contextual, to anticipate the availability conversation with the patient — it should not be used to exclude an option from the clinical list. Interaction with GLP-1/GIP agonists: the gastric emptying delay induced by semaglutide/tirzepatide (more pronounced with the latter) may reduce absorption of oral HRT — in patients on GLP-1/GIP therapy, prefer the transdermal route for estrogen therapy (same pharmacokinetic principle as in the Contraception during tirzepatide guide). Order of pharmacologic treatment for vasomotor symptoms (ACP 2026): 1st line — estrogen + progestogen with a uterus, or estrogen alone without a uterus (strong recommendation, high certainty). 2nd line, if contraindicated or not tolerated — SNRI: desvenlafaxine or venlafaxine. 3rd line — SSRI (escitalopram or paroxetine), gabapentin or NK antagonists (fezolinetant or elinzanetant): see Fezolinetant and elinzanetant. Shared decision: benefits, harms, comorbidities, preferences, cost and availability. National adaptation (MSPyBS Paraguay, Res. S.G. No. 267/2023): the Technical Guidelines for Comprehensive Care of Women in the Climacteric use the MRS adapted from MINSAL Chile. Total score ≥15: quality of life severely compromised. With a total ≥15, or severity in any domain, consider MHT if the woman wishes and has no contraindications. The document sets no per-domain cutoffs. The psychological domain does not diagnose depression. ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 13 (November 2026; replaces Practice Bulletin 141; doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000006428): systemic MHT — strong recommendation for vasomotor symptoms and related sleep disturbance, initiated before age 60 or within 10 years of menopause. Conjugated estrogens + bazedoxifene: conditional. Non-hormonal: SSRIs/SNRIs, strong; NK receptor antagonists, strong (moderate-to-high evidence); gabapentin, conditional, when other non-hormonal options fail. CBT, mindfulness, exercise, hypnosis and acupuncture: conditional. Insufficient evidence for MHT in depressive symptoms (major depressive disorder is treated per depression guidelines). Unscheduled bleeding on MHT: requires evaluation. Discontinuation: individualized. Phytoestrogens and herbal supplements are not among the recommended options. Unlike ACP 2026, ACOG does not rank options by line.

novedades.fuentes: WHO Semen Manual (6th ed., 2021) · WHO Infertility Guideline 2025 · AUA/ASRM 2024 · EAU · ESHRE RPL 2022 · ESHRE RIF 2023 · Heller and Clermont 1964
novedades.texto: WHO 2021 lower reference limits (5th percentile): volume 1.4 mL · concentration 16 M/mL · total 39 M per ejaculate · total motility 42 % · progressive 30 % · normal forms 4 % · vitality 54 %. Nomenclature: hypospermia (low volume) · oligozoospermia (low concentration or total) · asthenozoospermia (low progressive) · teratozoospermia (low normal forms) · necrozoospermia (low vitality) · OAT (all three) · cryptozoospermia (only in the centrifuged pellet) · azoospermia (none after centrifugation). Management: normal result: one test is enough. Abnormal: repeat after ≥11 weeks (WHO 2025) and refer to urology/andrology with physical exam, FSH and testosterone. Concentration <5 M/mL with high FSH or testicular atrophy: karyotype; ≤1 M/mL or non-obstructive azoospermia: Y-chromosome microdeletions (AUA/ASRM 2024). Azoospermia: volume, pH and FSH; absent vas deferens → CFTR testing. Low volume: post-ejaculatory urinalysis and rule out obstruction. TMSC (total motile sperm after processing) — CaVeSal® suggestion: >3–5 M → IUI · 1–3 M → IVF · <1 M → direct ICSI. Fewer than 5 M motile sperm after processing lowers IUI success (AUA/ASRM 2024). Spermatogenic window and sperm DNA fragmentation: spermatogenesis lasts about 74 days (Heller and Clermont 1964), plus epididymal transit: about 72–90 days in total; lifestyle or treatment changes show in semen after about 3 months, hence repeating after ≥11 weeks (WHO 2025). Recurrent pregnancy loss: evaluate the male partner with sperm DNA fragmentation (AUA/ASRM 2024, moderate, grade C) and karyotype (expert opinion); ESHRE 2022: may be considered for explanatory purposes (conditional), using a validated method, with no reference test. Recurrent implantation failure: not recommended (ESHRE 2023). Normal semen analysis without recurrent loss: not routine (ESHRE 2023). Maternal KIR/paternal HLA-C: research only, not for diagnosis or treatment (ESHRE 2022). Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Couple workup).

novedades.titulo: Fezolinetant and elinzanetant — NK receptor antagonists, non-hormonal therapy for vasomotor symptoms
novedades.fuentes: Pratt MC, et al. Expert Rev Clin Pharmacol 2023;16(5):389-398 · Panay N, et al. Climacteric 2024;27(3):221-235 · ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 13. Obstet Gynecol. 2026;148(5):e345-e369 (Table 2) · Qaseem A, et al. ACP. Ann Intern Med 2026. doi:10.7326/ANNALS-26-01205
novedades.texto: Mechanism: neurokinin receptor antagonists that act on hypothalamic KNDy neurons involved in thermoregulation, with no hormonal action. Fezolinetant: selective NK3 antagonist. Elinzanetant: dual NK1/NK3 antagonist. Fezolinetant: 45mg PO once daily, with or without food. FDA-approved for vasomotor symptoms (VMS). ⚠️ FDA boxed warning: requires baseline liver function testing, repeated monthly during the first 3 months of use, and again at 6 and 9 months. Elinzanetant: 120mg PO once daily. FDA-approved for VMS and also for menopause-related sleep disturbance (a sleep benefit not included in fezolinetant's specific approval). Requires liver function testing before starting and again at 3 months of treatment — a less intensive monitoring cadence than fezolinetant. Indication (both): moderate-to-severe VMS of the climacteric, a non-hormonal alternative when HRT is contraindicated or not the patient's preference (hormone-dependent cancer history, VTE, personal preference). In indirect network comparisons (ACOG CPG13), both drugs show similar efficacy on VMS frequency and severity; elinzanetant showed a greater effect on sleep disturbance (PROMIS sleep disturbance score) in indirect comparison with fezolinetant. Most common adverse effects vs. placebo in the OASIS trials with elinzanetant: headache and fatigue. Place in treatment (ACP 2026): 3rd line (moderate certainty), after HRT and SNRIs (desvenlafaxine or venlafaxine), alongside SSRIs and gabapentin. See MRS Scale and Hormone Replacement Therapy. ACOG 2026 (CPG No. 13): NK receptor antagonists — strong recommendation (moderate-to-high evidence) for vasomotor symptoms and related sleep disturbance, when hormones are not desired or are contraindicated.

novedades.fuentes: Amor F et al. J Ultrasound Med 2009;28:285-291 · UOG 2011;38:450-455 · meta-analysis PubMed 36790399
novedades.texto: Categories: 1 normal ovaries (0 %) · 2 very probably benign, functional: follicle, corpus luteum, hemorrhagic cyst (<1 %) · 3 probably benign, non-functional: endometrioma, dermoid, simple cyst, hydrosalpinx, paraovarian cyst, inclusion cyst, pedunculated fibroid (1–4 %) · 4 probably malignant, one or two malignancy features (5–20 %) · 5 very probably malignant, three or more features (>20 %). Malignancy features: thick papillary projections, thick septa, solid areas, ascites, central vascularization, resistance index <0.5. Management: 1–2 no follow-up or follow-up; 3 general gynecologist; 4–5 markers (CA-125, CEA, AFP/hCG/LDH if <40), contrast MRI or CT as appropriate, and referral to gynecologic oncology. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Adnexal mass).

novedades.fuentes: WHO. WHO labour care guide: user’s manual. Geneva: WHO; 2021. Spanish ed. ISBN 978-92-4-002853-1 · Licence CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO · Own summary; does not reproduce the form
novedades.texto: What it is: a WHO tool that replaces the classic partograph. It is used from the start of the active phase (5 cm) and through the second stage. It records supportive care, the baby’s condition, the woman’s condition, labour progress, medication and shared decision-making. Progress — alert values in the active phase (time at the same dilatation): 5 cm ≥6 h; 6 cm ≥5 h; 7 cm ≥3 h; 8 cm ≥2.5 h; 9 cm ≥2 h. If labour progresses as expected, vaginal examination every 4 h. Second stage: ≥3 h in nulliparous women; ≥2 h in multiparous women. Contractions: alert with ≤2 or >5 in 10 minutes, or duration <20 or >60 seconds. Baby: baseline fetal heart rate <110 or ≥160 bpm. Auscultation every 30 minutes in the first stage and every 5 minutes in the second stage. Woman: pulse <60 or ≥120 bpm; systolic pressure <80 or ≥140 mmHg; diastolic ≥90 mmHg; temperature <35.0 or ≥37.5 °C. Supportive care: companion of choice, pain relief, oral fluids and freedom of position. Not offering them is also an alert value. When an alert value appears, the guide calls for assessing, recording and planning the action with the woman. Evidence shows wide variation in dilatation patterns, so a threshold alone is not an indication to intervene.

novedades.fuentes: ATA 2017 · Endocrine Society · Lazarus JH et al. NEJM 2012 (CATS) · Casey BM et al. NEJM 2017 · Dhillon-Smith RK et al. NEJM 2019 (TABLET)
novedades.texto: Anti-TPO+ (>34 IU/mL) + TSH above range: Hashimoto's, start levothyroxine. Anti-TPO+ with TSH 2.5–4.0: consider levothyroxine (ATA 2017). Anti-TPO+ with normal TSH: recheck every 4–6 wk (2–5x risk of gestational hypothyroidism). The TABLET trial (2019) showed no benefit of levothyroxine in euthyroid anti-TPO+ women. Preconception (ATA 2017): treated hypothyroid women, adjust to TSH between the lower limit and 2.5. IVF/ICSI with subclinical hypothyroidism: levothyroxine with a TSH goal <2.5 (rec. 20). Confirmed pregnancy on prior treatment: +25–30% starting dose. Neurodevelopment: CATS (2012) and Casey (2017) showed no benefit of treating subclinical hypothyroidism on child IQ. Anti-Tg: isolated positive anti-Tg also indicates thyroid autoimmunity, but the ATA 2017 levothyroxine decision is based on anti-TPO. With positive anti-Tg, check TSH once pregnancy is confirmed.

novedades.titulo: Urinary incontinence — Stress vs. urge and management
novedades.fuentes: AUA/SUFU SUI 2023 · AUA/SUFU OAB 2024 · NICE NG123 (2019) · Stamey TA. Ann Surg 1980 · Sandvik H et al. 1993 y 2000
novedades.texto: Type: stress (cough, laughter, exercise; small volume; urethral hypermobility or sphincter deficiency) · urge (sudden desire, frequency, nocturia; detrusor overactivity) · mixed: treat the most bothersome component first. Rule out infection, retention (high post-void residual), haematuria, pain, mass, prior surgery or radiotherapy, neurological symptoms: refer. Stamey (stress): 0 continent · 1 with coughing, sneezing or lifting · 2 with light effort (walking, standing up) · 3 total, in any position. Sandvik: frequency (1–4) × amount (1–3): 1–2 slight · 3–6 moderate · 8–9 severe · 12 very severe. Bladder diary (3 days): >8 daytime voids, frequency · nocturia 2 or more · polyuria >40 ml/kg/24 h · nocturnal polyuria >20 % (under 65) or >33 % (65 or older) of daily volume. Management: weight loss, fluid and caffeine adjustment, treat constipation; vaginal estrogen if atrophy. Stress: supervised pelvic floor muscle training for 3 months, pessary or intravaginal device, duloxetine 40 mg twice daily if surgery is declined; surgery: midurethral sling (TVT/TOT), Burch colposuspension, autologous sling or bulking agents. Urge: bladder training; β3 agonists (mirabegron 25–50 mg/day, vibegron 75 mg/day) or antimuscarinics (solifenacin 5–10 mg/day, extended-release oxybutynin 5–30 mg/day); avoid anticholinergics in older women. Refractory: onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U intravesical, percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS) or sacral neuromodulation. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Incontinence).

novedades.titulo: Ovulation induction — Cancellation criteria and OHSS prevention
novedades.fuentes: ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034 · ASRM Practice Committee (2013), Fertil Steril 100:341-348
novedades.texto: In low-complexity techniques (timed intercourse/IUI), the safety threshold requires strictly avoiding high-order multiple pregnancy and Ovarian Hyperstimulation Syndrome (OHSS). Immediate cancellation criteria — do NOT give hCG: ≥3 mature follicles (≥15-16mm) in women <35 years, or >3-4 mature follicles in any low-complexity patient. More than 4-6 intermediate follicles (11-14mm) that could respond to the trigger. Serum estradiol >1,000-1,500pg/mL (if measured). Management on cancellation: cancel and withhold the hCG trigger (it is the direct trigger for the VEGF cascade and capillary hyperpermeability of OHSS). Advise strict coital abstinence or mandatory condom use for ≥7-10 days. Do not give hCG for luteal support. Rescue option at a high-complexity center: convert the cycle to IVF with follicular aspiration, GnRH-agonist trigger, and total embryo cryopreservation ("freeze-all").

novedades.titulo: Ovulation induction — Follicular size for the hCG trigger
novedades.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2013), Fertil Steril 100:341-348 · ASRM Practice Committee (2020), Fertil Steril 113:66-70 · Palatnik et al. (2012), Fertil Steril 97:1089-1094 · Shalom-Paz et al. (2014), Gynecol Endocrinol 30(2):107-110 · Ling et al. (2024), Eur J Med Res 29:184 · Van Oirschot et al. (2025), Fertil Steril · ESHRE Ovarian Stimulation Guideline (2025) · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034
novedades.texto: The hCG trigger mimics the endogenous LH surge: it resumes oocyte meiosis, luteinizes the granulosa cells, and times follicular rupture (36-40h after administration). Trigger agents: Recombinant hCG (r-hCG) 250mcg SC · urinary hCG (u-hCG) 5,000-10,000 IU IM. Follicular size by inducing agent: Clomiphene citrate: trigger with the leading follicle at a mean diameter of 20-28mm; ASRM notes higher pregnancy rates at 23-28mm (follicles under clomiphene mature at larger diameters: in conception cycles the leading follicle measured 20.4 ± 1.2mm). Monitor endometrial thickness because of the antiestrogenic effect. Letrozole: trigger with the leading follicle at 19-23mm (optimal 19.1-21mm in the first IUI cycle); tolerated up to 28mm. Gonadotropins (FSH/hMG): trigger with the leading follicle at 16-18mm (oocyte maturity is reached at slightly smaller sizes under direct gonadotropins; triggering above 19-20mm increases oocyte senescence). Note: ESHRE (2025) considers that the association between follicle size and outcome has not been sufficiently studied; the trigger size is individualized. Concurrent endometrial status: ideally ≥7mm with a trilaminar pattern before ordering the trigger. Timing of intercourse/insemination: timed intercourse — the night of the trigger and again 36h later (or on alternating days: trigger day and the next). IUI — sperm preparation and insemination at 36h (range 34-38h) post-hCG.

novedades.titulo: Ovulation induction — Therapeutic choice: Letrozole vs. Clomiphene vs. Gonadotropins
novedades.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2013), Fertil Steril 100:341-348 · Teede et al., Int'l PCOS Guideline (2023), Fertil Steril 120(4):767-793 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034 · MSPyBS Paraguay (2025), Res. S.G. Nº 050/2025
novedades.texto: Letrozole (aromatase inhibitor) — first-line in PCOS/WHO Type II anovulation, especially with overweight/obesity (BMI≥25-30). Higher cumulative ovulation, clinical pregnancy and live-birth rates than clomiphene (PPCOS II trial). Does not block endometrial or cervical estrogen receptors (preserves endometrial thickness and cervical mucus quality). Short half-life (~48h): favors monofollicular development, lower multiple-pregnancy rate. Clomiphene citrate (SERM): first-line alternative when letrozole is unavailable/not tolerated, or in unexplained infertility (timed intercourse/IUI). Drawback: prolonged peripheral antiestrogenic effect (half-life >2 weeks) — refractory thin endometrium (<7mm) and hostile mucus; higher multifollicular/multiple-pregnancy rate (5-10%, mostly twins) than letrozole. Exogenous gonadotropins (recombinant FSH / hMG): failure or resistance to oral agents (after 3-6 ovulatory cycles without conception); or Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism (WHO Type I — hypothalamic-pituitary axis not intact, clomiphene/letrozole do NOT work, requires hMG or FSH+hCG/LH microdose); or as an adjunct in low-complexity/IUI cycles.

novedades.titulo: Ovulation induction — Dosing regimens and stimulation protocols
novedades.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2013), Fertil Steril 100:341-348 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034 · MSPyBS Paraguay (2025), Res. S.G. Nº 050/2025
novedades.texto: Letrozole: 2.5mg/day PO x5 days, starting cycle day 2-5. If no ovulation, escalate to 5.0mg/day the next cycle; maximum dose 7.5mg/day x5 days. Clomiphene citrate: 50mg/day PO x5 days, day 2-5. If no response, increase to 100mg/day; usual maximum 150mg/day x5 days (higher doses do not improve pregnancy rates and worsen the endometrial antiestrogenic effect). Limit: 6 ovulatory cycles. Gonadotropins — "Low-Dose Step-Up" protocol: strict goal of monofollicular development and OHSS prevention. Starting dose 37.5-50-75 IU/day SC/IM from cycle day 2-3, holding the fixed dose for 7-14 days. If after 14 days there is no follicular selection (no follicle ≥10mm), increase 50% weekly (e.g. 37.5→75 IU/day) until a response is seen, then maintain that dose through the trigger.

novedades.titulo: Ovulation induction — Treatment failure and drug resistance
novedades.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2013), Fertil Steril 100:341-348
novedades.texto: Drug resistance: persistent absence of recruitment, or no follicles ≥15mm despite maximum doses. Clomiphene resistance: anovulation after 150mg/day x5 days. Letrozole resistance: anovulation after 7.5mg/day x5 days. Management: switch therapeutic line (CC→Letrozole, add Metformin in PCOS with insulin resistance, or move to low-dose gonadotropins). Failed induction (treatment failure): confirmed regular ovulatory cycles (optimal follicular development, follicular rupture and adequate luteal phase with progesterone ≥10ng/mL) without pregnancy after 4-6 consecutive ovulatory cycles. Management: full couple re-evaluation (tubal patency by HSG if not yet done, repeat semen analysis with TMSC) and escalation to high-complexity ART (IVF/ICSI). Endometrial failure (antiestrogenic effect): adequate follicular growth but persistently thin endometrium (<6-7mm) in the preovulatory window (common with clomiphene). Management: switch to letrozole or add exogenous estrogen support.

novedades.titulo: Ovulation induction — Baseline and serial ultrasound monitoring
novedades.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2013), Fertil Steril 100:341-348 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034
novedades.texto: Baseline transvaginal ultrasound + Antral Follicle Count (AFC), cycle days 2-4 — mandatory before starting any inducing agent: thin, shed endometrium (<5mm); rule out functional cysts/persistent follicles from the previous cycle (start if no follicles/cysts >10mm; postpone/cancel if a residual cyst or growing follicle ≥10-15mm is found, usually with baseline E2 >50-60pg/mL). AFC (bilateral 2-9mm follicles): <5-7 suggests low ovarian reserve · 8-15 normal reserve · ≥20 (or ovarian volume ≥10mL) polycystic ovarian morphology — maximum alert for hyperresponse and OHSS risk. Serial follow-up: first post-stimulation scan on cycle day 8-10, then every 48-72h depending on follicular growth rate (expected physiologic growth 1.5-2mm/day). Record the mean diameter in 2 perpendicular planes per ovary, and endometrial thickness/pattern (optimal: periovulatory trilaminar "triple line" ≥7-8mm).

novedades.titulo: Insulin resistance — HOMA-IR and OGTT in PMOS
novedades.fuentes: Matthews DR et al. Diabetologia 1985 · International PMOS Guideline 2023 (Teede) · ADA Standards of Care
novedades.texto: HOMA-IR = fasting glucose (mg/dL) × fasting insulin (µU/mL) / 405 (with glucose in mmol/L: / 22.5). Limitations: there is no universal cut-off; it varies by population, BMI and insulin assay. The 2023 international guideline does not recommend measuring insulin or insulin resistance indices in routine clinical practice. Use it only as descriptive data. Recommended (2023 guideline): assess glycemic status at diagnosis and every 1–3 years; 75 g OGTT in every woman with PMOS planning pregnancy or fertility treatment (if not feasible, fasting glucose or HbA1c). Outside pregnancy (ADA): fasting 100–125 mg/dL impaired fasting glucose, ≥126 diabetes; 2 h 140–199 impaired tolerance, ≥200 diabetes; HbA1c 5.7–6.4 % prediabetes, ≥6.5 % diabetes. Management: lifestyle for all; metformin in adults with BMI ≥25 for metabolic outcomes; the 2023 guideline considers inositol experimental (see "Myo-inositol"). Lipid profile and blood pressure. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (PMOS).

novedades.fuentes: ACR 2020 Reproductive Health Guideline (Sammaritano LR et al.) · SMFM Consult #64
novedades.texto: Timing: plan pregnancy with inactive or low-activity lupus for at least 6 months on compatible medication. Postpone after recent severe activity or severe organ damage. Prior labs: antiphospholipid antibodies (lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, anti-β2 glycoprotein I) and anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB; renal function and proteinuria. Medication (ACR 2020): continue or start hydroxychloroquine. Stop mycophenolate ≥6 weeks before, methotrexate 1–3 months before and cyclophosphamide 3 months before. Compatible: hydroxychloroquine, azathioprine, tacrolimus, cyclosporine and low-dose prednisone. Low-dose aspirin from the first trimester, ideally from 12 weeks, for preeclampsia risk. Positive anti-Ro/La: risk of congenital heart block; fetal rhythm surveillance per protocol. With APS: see "Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS) and thrombophilias". Team: counseling with maternal-fetal medicine and rheumatology before trying to conceive. Flagged in CaVeSal® GYN (Preconception).

novedades.fuentes: ACOG PB 171 · FIGO/WHO · NICE NG25
novedades.texto: Cutoffs by guideline: ACOG wk 24-33+6 (late 34-36+6) · FIGO/WHO 24-34+6 · NICE offer 24-33+6, consider 34-35+6. Regimens: Betamethasone 12mg IM q24h (2 doses) · Dexamethasone 6mg IM q12h (4 doses). Rescue course: if >14 days have passed, GA <34 wk, imminent risk within 7 days. In PROM, ACOG considers the evidence insufficient for or against: it may be considered, without delaying delivery.

novedades.titulo: Mammography and BI-RADS — Categories 4-6 and management
novedades.fuentes: ACR BI-RADS v2025 · ACOG PB 223 · ACR 2023 (high risk)
novedades.texto: BI-RADS 4 (>2-<95%): 4A (>2-≤10%) · 4B (>10-≤50%) · 4C (>50-<95%). Image-guided core needle biopsy with radiologic-pathologic concordance; discordant → repeat or surgical biopsy. 4A benign concordant: follow-up at 6 months. BI-RADS 5 (≥95%): spiculated mass, fine pleomorphic branching calcifications → biopsy and referral to breast surgery and oncology; staging (see Breast cancer — TNM staging). BI-RADS 6: proven malignancy → multidisciplinary team. High risk (BRCA, chest radiation before 30, lifetime risk ≥20 %): annual contrast MRI plus mammography.

novedades.titulo: Mammography and BI-RADS — Breast density and categories 0-3
novedades.fuentes: ACR BI-RADS v2025 · ACR Appropriateness Criteria (palpable mass) · ACOG PB 223/179 · USPSTF 2024 · FDA MQSA 2024
novedades.texto: Supplemental ultrasound: dense breasts (ACR C/D) according to risk, <30 years with palpable mass, cyst vs. solid. Density (ACR): A (fatty) · B (scattered) · C (heterogeneously dense) · D (extremely dense). C and D: notify the patient (FDA 2024); supplemental imaging by risk (ACR suggests it; USPSTF 2024: insufficient evidence). BI-RADS v2025 — category 0 split: 0 needs additional imaging → <30 years targeted ultrasound; ≥30 diagnostic mammography or tomosynthesis plus ultrasound · 0 needs prior studies → obtain them for comparison. 1 negative and 2 benign (0%): routine screening every 2 years from 40 to 74 (USPSTF 2024). 3 probably benign (>0-≤2%): follow-up at 6, 12 and 24 months; biopsy if it changes. Suspicious palpable mass with negative imaging: consider biopsy. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Breast, cervix and endometrium).

novedades.fuentes: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care. 2026 · NICE Guideline NG3. Diabetes in pregnancy · Rowan JA, Hague WM, Gao W, et al. (MiG Trial). N Engl J Med. 2008;358(19):2003-2015 · Rowan JA, et al. (MiG TOFU, offspring follow-up at 2 and 7-9 years). Diabetes Care 2011 / BMJ Open Diabetes Res Care 2018 · ADA/ALAD (see Gestational Diabetes guide)
novedades.texto: The approach to metformin once pregnancy is confirmed depends on why it was prescribed — it is not a single rule: PMOS with ovulation induction/insulin resistance: ADA 2026 (recommendation 15.22, level A): when metformin was used for PCOS and ovulation induction, stop it by the end of the first trimester at the latest. Many of these patients reach pregnancy already on metformin and/or myo-inositol as part of their baseline metabolic management (see the PMOS and Myo-inositol guides) — there is no teratogenicity signal for metformin requiring its immediate discontinuation upon confirming pregnancy, unlike GLP-1/GIP analogues (see the Inadvertent pregnancy guide). Prediabetes: individualize according to glycemic control and risk factors. ADA (2026 Standards of Care) does not position metformin as routine in isolated gestational prediabetes — its use follows the same individualization logic as in non-pregnant high-risk patients (elevated BMI, prior GDM, PMOS). NICE (NG3) is somewhat more permissive when risk factors for frank gestational diabetes coexist, where metformin may be anticipated as part of early management if glycemia warrants it — neither guideline indicates it routinely in isolated prediabetes without another risk factor. ADA 2026: metformin does not prevent gestational diabetes (meta-analysis of 11 RCTs). NICE NG3 (1.1.21): metformin may be used as an adjunct or alternative to insulin before and during pregnancy when the glycemic benefit outweighs potential harm. Pregestational diabetes: ADA prioritizes insulin as first-choice treatment (type 1 and, in most cases, type 2) due to metformin's transplacental passage and a preference for more predictable control; it reserves metformin as an adjunct in type 2 diabetes with high insulin resistance/high requirements, not as monotherapy. NICE (NG3) accepts metformin as first-line or adjunctive therapy in pregestational type 2 diabetes, adding insulin if the glycemic target is not reached — a stance more favorable to oral therapy than ADA's. Gestational diabetes: metformin as a second-line agent versus insulin per ADA (insulin as the preferred first line, metformin as an acceptable alternative after discussing transplacental passage with the patient); NICE (NG3) accepts metformin as a reasonable first line before insulin, barring contraindication or lack of response — see also the algorithm already described in the Gestational Diabetes guide. Summary of the ADA vs. NICE divergence: both agree that uncontrolled hyperglycemia, not metformin, is the real teratogen, but they differ in how much weight they give oral metformin versus insulin: ADA tends to favor insulin as first-line therapy in overt diabetes (pregestational and gestational), reserving metformin as an adjunct or an alternative discussed case by case; NICE accepts metformin more broadly as a reasonable first line in several scenarios. Neither guideline diverges on PMOS, where the decision is individualized for reasons unrelated to fetal safety. Key counseling point: the demonstrated teratogen in this context is uncontrolled hyperglycemia — not metformin itself. This should guide the decision not to abruptly stop an antidiabetic agent without an already-defined replacement plan (insulin or another scheme). Offspring follow-up (MiG TOFU): follow-up of the MiG trial children at 2 years (Diabetes Care 2011) and 7-9 years (BMJ Open Diabetes Res Care 2018) assessed body composition and metabolic outcomes after in-utero metformin exposure — with no signal of harm that would contraindicate its use in gestational diabetes; this is the longest-term support available for this specific indication.

novedades.titulo: Myo-inositol — PMOS, ovulation induction, and inadvertent exposure
novedades.fuentes: Facchinetti F, et al. Reduction of oocyte quality and clinical outcomes using myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol: an update, Expert Opin Drug Metab Toxicol (2020) · Unfer V, et al. Myo-inositol effects in women with PCOS: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, Endocr Connect (2017) · Cochrane: Inositol for subfertility associated with PCOS (Review, 2023 update) · ESHRE/ASRM/Monash PCOS Guideline (2023) · Poyatos-León R, et al. The effect of myo-inositol supplementation on gestational diabetes mellitus prevention: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Am J Obstet Gynecol. 2026;235(5):1024-1036. DOI 10.1016/j.ajog.2026.05.020 · Motuhifonua SK, et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2023;CD011507.pub3
novedades.texto: Mechanism: myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol are second messengers in the insulin signaling pathway — supplementation improves ovarian insulin sensitivity, reduces compensatory hyperinsulinemia, and thereby favors resumption of ovulatory cycles in PMOS. It is not a drug in the strict sense but a dietary nutrient/supplement, which shapes its reproductive safety profile (see the inadvertent exposure note below). Indication: ovulatory dysfunction in PMOS/metabolic phenotype, as an adjunct or alternative to metformin in patients with digestive intolerance to the latter; also used as an adjuvant in ovulation induction/IVF protocols to improve oocyte quality. Dose: the 2023 international PCOS guideline (Teede et al., practice point 4.7.4) states that specific types, doses or combinations of inositol cannot be recommended for lack of evidence, and considers it experimental in infertility (5.8.1). Trials often used 2-4 g/day of myo-inositol, sometimes with D-chiro-inositol 40:1, but that regimen comes from studies, not a guideline-recommended dose. If prescribed, agree on it with the patient according to her preferences and reassess at 3-6 months. Evidence: the Cochrane review (2023 update) on inositol for PMOS-associated subfertility finds low-to-moderate certainty evidence favoring a possible improvement in clinical pregnancy and ovulation rates versus placebo, with meta-analyses by Unfer et al. and Facchinetti et al. also showing benefit on metabolic parameters (HOMA-IR, androgen profile) — overall evidence quality remains limited by study size and heterogeneity. Inadvertent exposure during fertility recovery (relevant in women coming off tirzepatide/semaglutide who are improving their metabolic profile): as a physiological nutrient normally present in the diet rather than a synthetic molecule with dedicated teratogenicity studies, myo-inositol is not subject to the same preconception washout restrictions as GLP-1/GIP analogues — no teratogenic warning signal has been described with continued use during an unrecognized pregnancy, and it has in fact also been studied as a supplement for gestational diabetes prevention in at-risk populations. This does not exempt confirming the pregnancy and reassessing the overall therapeutic plan as soon as it is detected. Specific meta-analysis on myo-inositol and gestational diabetes prevention (Poyatos-León R, et al. Am J Obstet Gynecol. 2026;235(5):1024-1036. DOI 10.1016/j.ajog.2026.05.020): 12 randomized controlled trials, 4,765 women without preexisting diabetes (pregnant or planning conception within 6 months), search through April 2025. Myo-inositol supplementation substantially reduced the risk of gestational diabetes versus control (44% relative risk reduction), with no significant differences in hypertensive disorders, cesarean delivery, macrosomia, preterm birth, or neonatal hypoglycemia. Cochrane review on prevention of gestational diabetes (Motuhifonua et al. 2023, CD011507.pub3): 7 RCTs with 1,319 women overall; gestational diabetes in 6 RCTs with 1,140 (RR 0.53; 95% CI 0.31-0.90; very low certainty); hypertensive disorders in 5 RCTs with 1,052 (RR 0.34; 95% CI 0.19-0.61; low certainty). ⚠️ Cochrane shows a reduction in hypertensive disorders and Poyatos-León finds no difference: the hypertensive finding is not conclusive.

novedades.fuentes: FIGO PALM-COEIN (Munro MG et al. IJGO 2018) · STEP-W (Lasmar 2011; ISGE 2023) · ACOG PB 228 (2021) · ASRM 2017
novedades.texto: Type 0 pedunculated intracavitary · 1 sessile <50% intramural · 2 sessile ≥50% · 3 100% intramural (contacts endometrium) · 4 100% intramural (no contact) · 5 subserosal ≥50% · 6 subserosal <50% · 7 pedunculated subserosal · 8 other locations · 2-5 transmural. STEP-W (submucosal): size ≤2 / >2–5 / >5 cm = 0/1/2 · topography lower/middle/upper third = 0/1/2 · base ≤1/3, >1/3–2/3, >2/3 of the wall = 0/1/2 · penetration 0 / ≤50 % / >50 % = 0/1/2 · lateral wall +1. Group I (0–4) low complexity · II (5–6) complex: prior GnRH analogues or two-step surgery · III (7–9) alternatives to hysteroscopy. Management: asymptomatic, expectant. Symptomatic submucosal: hysteroscopic myomectomy. Types 3–5: medical treatment (LNG-IUS, GnRH antagonists with add-back, tranexamic acid), myomectomy, embolization or hysterectomy. Types 6–7: laparoscopy if symptomatic. Infertility: resect types 0–2 (ASRM 2017). Anemia: iron. Suspected sarcoma (rapid growth after menopause, heterogeneous, necrosis): contrast MRI with diffusion, avoid uncontained morcellation, gynecologic oncology. Calculated in CaVeSal® GYN (Uterus).

novedades.fuentes: AMMR (Asociación Mexicana de Medicina de la Reproducción). "The Incretin Pipeline" — Fig. 2: Current GLP-1 agonist anti-obesity medications and expected upcoming anti-obesity medications. Information from clinicaltrials.gov and/or company websites; presentation by Dr. Eduardo W. Goicochea · Garvey WT, et al. N Engl J Med 2025;393:635-647 (REDEFINE 1). doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2502081
novedades.texto: Quick-reference map of incretin agonists beyond the 3 already approved (semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide — see GLP-1/GIP analogs guide). None of the following yet has approval for general clinical use; they are listed for context and to anticipate patient questions, not as a use recommendation. Closest to approval (per the source's timeline, subject to change): Oral semaglutide: GLP-1, oral daily, Novo Nordisk. CagriSema (semaglutide + cagrilintide): GLP-1 + amylin analogue, SC weekly, Novo Nordisk. REDEFINE 1: −20.4% vs. −3.0% with placebo at 68 weeks (Garvey WT, et al. N Engl J Med 2025;393:635-647). Encoglutide (XW003): GLP-1, SC weekly, Sciwind (in development in China). Orforglipron (LY3502970): oral non-peptide GLP-1 agonist (GLP-1 only), oral daily, Eli Lilly. Mazdutide: GLP-1/glucagon receptor co-agonist, SC weekly, Eli Lilly/Innovent (in development in China). Survodutide (BI 456906): GLP-1/glucagon receptor co-agonist, SC weekly, Boehringer Ingelheim. Retatrutide (LY3437943): GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist, SC, Eli Lilly — this is the molecule mentioned in the Preconception washout guide as "under investigation." Pemvidutide: GLP-1/glucagon receptor co-agonist, SC weekly, Altimmune. Earlier-stage development / distinct mechanisms: Cagrilintide (AM833): long-acting amylin analogue (not GLP-1), SC weekly, Novo Nordisk. Amycretin: amylin receptor and GLP-1 co-agonist, SC and oral under investigation, Novo Nordisk. Maridebart cafraglutide (AMG-133): GLP-1 agonist + GIP receptor antagonist (antibody conjugate), SC monthly or less often, Amgen (phase 2: every 4 weeks; Jastreboff AM, et al. N Engl J Med 2025;393:843-857). Bimagrumab: monoclonal antibody blocking activin signaling (not an incretin agonist), IV infusion every 4 weeks, Versanis/Eli Lilly. Danuglipron: GLP-1 agonist, oral, Pfizer — discontinued development: after completing Phase 2, Phase 3 planning was cancelled due to hepatic adverse effects; kept in this list only as historical reference, not as an active candidate. APH-012 / SYNTH-101: oral capsule that simulates the effect of gastric bypass (duodenal lining, stimulates the small intestine), Phase 2 in development, APHAIA FARMA/SYNTIS BIO. ARD-101: oral agonist targeting taste receptors (denatonium), activates endogenous GLP-1/GLP-2/cholecystokinin, finishing Phase 2, Aardvark Therapeutics. CT-388: GLP-1/GIP co-agonist, SC weekly, Structure Therapeutics. VK2735: GLP-1/GIP co-agonist, SC weekly, Viking Pharmaceuticals. HU6: "controlled metabolic accelerator" (distinct mechanism, not an incretin), oral daily, Rivus Pharmaceuticals. INV-202: CB1 blocker, oral daily, Novo Nordisk. EC5004: GLP-1 agonist, oral daily, AstraZeneca/Eccogene. GSBR-1290: GLP-1 agonist, oral daily, Structure Therapeutics. ⚠️ None of these investigational molecules has, as of this guide, reproductive safety studies or a validated preconception washout recommendation — for any patient in a clinical trial with one of these, strictly follow the study's own contraception protocol; do not extrapolate the semaglutide/tirzepatide windows. Timeline and availability taken from the original source (clinicaltrials.gov and company websites, at the time of the presentation) — these can change; verify current regulatory status before discussing with a patient.

novedades.fuentes: ASRM Female Infertility Evaluation (2021) · ATA (2017) · ASRM 2026 · ESHRE POI 2024 · International PMOS Guideline 2023 (Teede)
novedades.texto: Early follicular (2-4): FSH <8-10 optimal, >15 low reserve. LH/FSH>2-3 suggests PCOS. AMH: optimal 1.2-3.5. Mid luteal (day 21): P4 ≥10 optimal. Thyroid: TSH target <2.5. Normal PRL <20-25. ASRM 2026 update: TSH and prolactin only with clinical indication (irregular cycles, galactorrhea, symptoms), not routinely. The LH/FSH ratio is not a diagnostic criterion for PMOS in the 2023 international guideline. Premature ovarian insufficiency (ESHRE 2024): <40 years, oligo/amenorrhea ≥4 months and one FSH >25 IU/L; repeat at 4–6 weeks only if in doubt. Counseling: oocyte donation as a pregnancy option and hormone therapy until the age of natural menopause.

novedades.titulo: Newborn screening and neonatal discharge summary
novedades.fuentes: MSPBS Neonatal Care Manual 2016 (Res. S.G. No. 816) · MSPBS Early Hearing Loss Detection Guide 2020 (Res. S.G. No. 063/2020) · Law 2138/2003 · Law 5732/2016 · AAP 2025 (Oster et al.) · ACOG CO 644 · ACOG/AAP 2014
novedades.texto: Neonatal discharge summary (minimum data): gestational age and prematurity category (WHO: extremely preterm <28 wk, very preterm 28–31+6, moderate or late 32–36+6), birth weight and category (low <2500 g, very low <1500 g, extremely low <1000 g), weight percentile entered manually (INTERGROWTH-21st), Apgar at 1 and 5 minutes (ACOG CO 644: 7–10 reassuring, 4–6 moderately abnormal, 0–3 low), cord gases (pH <7.0 or base deficit ≥12 mmol/L: significant acidemia, ACOG/AAP 2014), resuscitation, admission and each screening result. Heel-prick test: mandatory in Paraguay (Law 2138/2003; National Newborn Screening Program, Law 5732/2016). Filter-paper sample before discharge, between 24 hours and day 7 of life. Abnormal result: follow the Program's recall. Hearing (otoacoustic emissions, OAE): universal, before discharge or within the first month (Manual 2016). Hearing Loss Guide 2020: up to 3 OAE. No hearing risk factors and not passing: 2nd OAE at 30 days and 3rd at 3 months; if persistent, refer to ENT for evoked potentials (ABR/ASSR). With risk factors: 2nd OAE at 30 days even if the first one passed. Red reflex: ophthalmoscope, dark room, 30–45 cm, both eyes at once.
